items.title: 南海：菲律宾周边军演与中国海军活动叠加
items.description: 南海方向出现新的军事活动信号。WIRE 信息显示，在“肩并肩”联合军演背景下，中国海军在菲律宾附近海域的部署受到关注。对中国周边安全来说，这类动态的敏感点不在单次行动，而在军事存在、演训频率和外部力量介入是否持续上升。
items.rawSummary: Mayon Volcano erupted massively with Alert Level 3 in effect, and a subsequent lava flow collapse triggered a pyroclastic density current that hurled ash toward Legazpi City, raising concerns in Albay province.
items.analysis: A massive eruption occurred at Mayon Volcano, with Alert Level 3 maintained due to the heightened risk of hazardous activity. A subsequent lava flow collapse triggered a pyroclastic density current, sending ash plumes visible from Legazpi City, which raised concerns over air quality, transport, and agriculture in Albay. There were no immediate reports of casualties or evacuation orders.

keyPoints.point: A massive eruption occurred at Mayon Volcano; Alert Level 3 remains in effect.
A lava flow collapse generated a fast-moving pyroclastic density current, with ash plumes visible from Legazpi City and concerns over air quality, transport, and agriculture in Albay.

items.title: 北京外交：零关税、台湾议题与对日摩擦同时推进
items.description: 中国相关动态今天集中在外交和经贸层面。WIRE 信息显示，中国对 53 个非洲国家的进口零关税政策生效，同时因台湾承认问题将斯威士兰排除在外；中美围绕技术和古巴制裁的摩擦仍在延续，中日之间关于军事言论的交锋也没有降温。这说明北京正在同时处理经贸拉拢、台湾议题和大国竞争三条线。
items.rawSummary: As a U.S. military aircraft arrived in Beijing to prepare for a mid-May Trump-Xi summit, Chinese authorities instructed domestic companies to defy U.S. sanctions on oil refiners that buy Iranian oil, part of a broader wave of assertive actions that also saw Beijing block a Meta acquisition, sharply rebuke Japan, grant zero-tariff access to African nations excluding Eswatini, and press Washington to rescind Cuba sanctions.
items.analysis: The zero-tariff policy for African nations, now in effect, excludes Eswatini to reinforce Beijing's One-China stance. Blocking Meta's acquisition of Manus extends technology tensions with the U.S., while the sharp rebuke of Japan over perceived military moves heightens regional security rhetoric. China's Foreign Ministry also urged the U.S. to walk back its Cuba sanctions regime, accusing it of vilifying China-Cuba cooperation. In a further move, Beijing declared it does not recognize U.S. sanctions on Iranian oil purchases and will not comply, and its Ministry of Commerce has now instructed Chinese companies not to adhere to sanctions on oil refiners, calling the measures illegal extraterritorial overreach. Separately, a U.S. military C-17 aircraft landed in Beijing to prepare for a mid-May summit between President Trump and President Xi, adding a layer of diplomatic engagement to the current assertive policy landscape.

keyPoints.point: China blocks Meta's $2 billion acquisition of AI firm Manus.

China's Foreign Ministry accuses Japan of making dangerous, provocative moves, likening its actions to 'war mobilization and war cries,' and questions whether Japan seeks to repeat history as a source of disaster in East Asia.
China announces tariff-free access for all African countries with diplomatic ties to Beijing, excluding Eswatini because it recognizes Taiwan.
China's Foreign Ministry urges the U.S. to walk back its sanctions regime against Cuba, accusing the U.S. of 'vilifying China-Cuba cooperation.'
China's zero-tariff policy on imports from 53 African countries takes effect; Eswatini is excluded because it recognizes Taiwan.
China states it does not recognize U.S. sanctions on Iranian oil purchases and will not comply with them.
A U.S. military C-17 aircraft lands in Beijing as preparations begin for a meeting between President Trump and President Xi on May 14-15.
China's Ministry of Commerce tells Chinese companies not to comply with U.S. sanctions on certain oil refiners, calling the sanctions illegal extraterritorial overreach.

items.title: 伊朗战局：美方宣称敌对行动终止，但军事压力并未消失
items.description: 尽管美国以战争权力程序为由声称敌对状态已经结束，WIRE 信息显示，海上封锁仍在继续冲击伊朗经济，美方也仍在讨论潜在的进一步军事选项。与此同时，伊朗内部路线分歧和强硬表态交织，使局势离真正降温仍有距离。
items.rawSummary: Iran has submitted a new 14-point two-stage peace proposal to the U.S., while economic devastation from the naval blockade deepens, diplomatic deadlock persists, and President Trump remains dissatisfied, threatening further military action.
items.analysis: The U.S. naval blockade continues to devastate Iran's economy, with oil storage approaching capacity and the rial at record lows, prompting Iran to reduce production to avoid field damage. Diplomatic efforts remain deadlocked: President Trump, briefed on 'final blow' strike options and dissatisfied with Iran's latest proposal, has acknowledged a 'possibility' of resuming strikes, and wants to eliminate the remaining 15% of Iran's missile-making capabilities. Channel 12 reported that Israeli Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir is intensifying contacts with CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper on potential military action, signaling growing Israeli coordination. Iranian leaders remain defiant, with Supreme Leader Khamenei vowing to sink American ships and Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf mocking the blockade, while the Washington Post reported that the security establishment rejects compromise on enrichment and Iran exploits the ceasefire to recover hidden weapons. Axios reported on May 3 that Iran submitted a 14-point proposal outlining a two-stage plan: first, negotiate a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, lift the blockade, and end wars in Iran and Lebanon; then, begin separate talks on the nuclear program, indicating a more structured diplomatic approach even as the U.S. maintains maximum pressure. The war's toll extends to the U.S., where surging jet fuel prices derailed Spirit Airlines' bankruptcy exit, and a new Washington Post–ABC–Ipsos poll shows 61% of Americans now view the conflict as a mistake. Strikes disrupted IRGC-linked cryptocurrency mining, temporarily stabilizing electricity, and Hezbollah's footage of domestic drone production adds a regional dimension to the conflict.

keyPoints.point: Reports emerge of deep divisions within Iranian leadership between hardline IRGC generals who view negotiations as futile under the U.S. blockade and political figures who argue for a negotiated settlement to relieve economic pressure, with the hardliners currently prevailing.
Mojtaba Khamenei remains in hiding surrounded by military staff, having delegated significant autonomy to extreme IRGC generals who are pushing hardline negotiating positions.

The New York Times reports, citing Iranian officials, that Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is gravely wounded from an earlier strike, having undergone multiple leg surgeries, suffered facial burns, and is slowly regaining function, communicating only through sealed handwritten messages relayed by couriers.

The New York Times reports that Khamenei's delegation of decision-making powers to his generals, due to his incapacitation, has allowed them to gain disproportionate influence in Iran's decision-making process.
Iranian Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf reportedly resigns from Iran's negotiating team following IRGC intervention, further consolidating hardliner control over diplomatic channels.
President Trump issues a public warning to Iran, stating 'the clock is ticking' and asserting he has all the time in the world while Iran does not.
Pro-regime Iranian journalists deny reports that Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf has resigned from the negotiating team, creating a discrepancy in assessment of the internal power struggle.

The U.S. has expended over 1,000 Tomahawk missiles and 1,500-2,000 critical air-defense missiles since the war began, so depleting stockpiles that Trump administration officials assess the U.S. could not fully defend Taiwan from a Chinese invasion in the near term, and Zelensky notes the U.S. used the equivalent of two years' production of Patriot missiles in the first day alone.
Iran has deployed additional mines in the Strait of Hormuz, according to an Axios report.

President Trump states the U.S. ships are 'locked and loaded, ready to go' and that Iran has 'all new leadership' and is 'fighting like cats and dogs,' while declining to specify a timeline for negotiation.

Trump states the U.S. has hit about 75 percent of its targets and that a blockade is 100 percent effective, but also that Iran wants a deal and the U.S. has been speaking to them, though Tehran does not know who is leading the country.
Trump says 'we don't know who the leader is in Iran' and references regime change, further highlighting the confusion over Iranian leadership.
Trump acknowledges the war has lasted eight weeks despite his initial 4–6 week projection, stating he 'took a little break.'
Trump warns that if Iran used the two-week hiatus to reload, the U.S. 'will knock that out in about one day.'

U.S. military planners develop options to strike Iranian military leaders and other 'obstructionists' within the regime who are reportedly undermining negotiations, with IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi on the list.
President Trump states that Iran must stop funding Hezbollah as a condition for any deal.

U.S. military planners are preparing plans to strike Iran's defenses around the Strait of Hormuz if the current ceasefire fails, with potential targets including small attack boats, mine-laying vessels, missiles, and drones.

The U.S. has expended roughly 1,100 JASSM-ER cruise missiles, over 1,200 Patriot interceptors, and more than 1,000 ATACMS and Precision Strike missiles since late February, costing about $5.6 billion in the first two days, with the Pentagon redirecting weapons from Europe and Asia and substantially reducing readiness in both regions.
CNN reports the US is considering assassination strikes against specific Iranian leaders thought to be blocking US–Iran negotiations, with IRGC commander-in-chief Ahmad Vahidi on the list.
Iran's internet blackout reaches 56 consecutive days, with international connectivity severed for more than 1,320 hours, according to NetBlocks.
Trump administration freezes $344 million in cryptocurrency tied to Iran.
The US announces new Iran-related sanctions targeting a Chinese oil refinery, 19 tankers, and multiple crypto wallets used by the Central Bank of Iran.
Iranian media reports that no decision has been taken on whether the country will engage in another round of talks with the United States, signaling continued uncertainty over the diplomatic path.
The Senate Armed Services Committee Chair urges the Trump administration to resume strikes on Iran, reflecting growing congressional pressure to escalate military operations.
Suspicious drone and fighter jet activity was reported over several Iranian regions, likely indicating ISR or pre-targeting missions associated with planned decapitation strikes.
President Trump states there is 'tremendous infighting inside Iran' and they are 'probably fighting for leadership,' reinforcing the assessment of a deep internal power struggle.
Trump offers that Iran can call him, asserting the U.S. 'has all the cards' and 'won everything.'
Trump claims that Iran's initial negotiating paper was inadequate and that after he canceled it, a much-improved paper was received within ten minutes, indicating rapid concessions under pressure.
Trump states that Iran 'offered a lot, but not enough,' signaling that the U.S. perceives progress in negotiations but remains unsatisfied.

Iranian Special Police Forces release a propaganda video showing a fighter armed with a DIO TK9 'Tondar' submachine gun and warning 'We are waiting for you, with our hands on the trigger,' signaling combat readiness and defiance in the face of U.S. strike planning.

The Wall Street Journal reports that the U.S. has begun signaling it will allow some Iranian enrichment in negotiations, demanding a 20-year suspension but open to enrichment in the second decade, while Iran has countered with a 5-year suspension request.
German Chancellor Merz calls the US-Iran conflict a 'completely unnecessary war,' marking a high-level international critique of the hostilities.
Iran executes a man over accusations of armed rebellion and alleged membership in the Sunni resistance group Jaish al-Adl, signaling continued internal repression amid the conflict.
President Trump declares that the Iran war will end very soon and the U.S. will be very victorious, projecting confidence despite the complex and unresolved situation on the ground.

Trump issues a three-day ultimatum, warning that Iran's oil infrastructure will be destroyed within that timeframe, significantly escalating the coercive pressure and setting a near-term deadline for compliance.

President Trump states the U.S. will 'take Iran's nuclear dust' as part of negotiations, demanding the complete removal of Iran's fissile material, a position which may undercut earlier signals of limited future enrichment.

Trump further hardens preconditions, stating Iran must forgo nuclear weapons entirely or there is no basis for talks, effectively closing the door to any negotiation that leaves even a latent weapons capability.

Pope Leo explicitly condemns the Iranian regime for mass-murder of protesters and executions, marking a high-level moral critique of the regime's internal repression and adding to international pressure.

Iran has made a new proposal to the United States, according to an Axios report, signaling continued diplomatic maneuvering despite Trump's hardened preconditions and the looming oil infrastructure ultimatum.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen states that it is too early to lift sanctions, demanding a fundamental change in Iran's human rights record, particularly women's rights, before any sanctions relief.

Vice President JD Vance raises significant concerns in Pentagon meetings about the amount of munitions used in the war and questions whether Iran's capabilities remain truly degraded but intact, while Defense Secretary Hegseth insists on the success of operations and solid stockpiles.

President Trump believes Iran is not acting in good faith and is failing to meet his key term of zero nuclear enrichment, according to the Wall Street Journal, further imperiling the diplomatic track.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio states that sanctions and pressure on the Islamic regime are extraordinary and that more can be brought to bear, signaling potential additional economic coercion.
U.S. Treasury Secretary says Iranian Revolutionary Guards leaders are 'trapped like drowning rats' and warns of impending gasoline shortages in Iran, underscoring the severe economic squeeze.

Iran's new proposal reportedly would not force immediate concessions on highly enriched uranium or enrichment capability, instead granting more time for negotiations, and IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi's support for the proposal is unclear.

Bloomberg reports that Iran is running out of onshore oil storage capacity with only 12 to 22 days remaining, as the U.S. naval blockade has cut exports by roughly 70% and nearly halted tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz; Iran may be forced to cut production by another 1.5 million barrels per day by mid-May, though financial impacts will be delayed.
The New York Times reports, citing European intelligence, that Russia is preparing to deliver highly advanced drones to Iran.
The Wall Street Journal reports that the U.S. naval blockade has cut Iranian crude loadings from about 2.1 million barrels per day to 567,000 barrels per day.
Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić states that the attack on Iran is a violation of international law, joining high-level international criticism of the conflict.
Washington was expected to reject Iran's peace proposal, with some predictions suggesting a resumption of strikes soon.

Axios reports that Trump is weighing two paths: escalating with military strikes or continuing maximum pressure sanctions; advisers describe him as frustrated but cautious about launching new attacks.

Bloomberg reports that Asian countries dependent on Iranian oil are already witnessing their worst energy crisis in history, which is expected to intensify as Iranian storage and production cuts deepen.
President Trump states that Iran has informed the United States it is in a 'State of Collapse' and wants the Strait of Hormuz opened as soon as possible while it resolves its leadership situation.

Intelligence reports indicate Iran has used the ceasefire to redeploy and unbury many of its drone and missile capabilities, spreading them across the country in preparation for a continuation of mass strikes.

Iran's April 26 proposal reportedly offers no concessions and reflects IRGC commander Vahidi's belief that Iran is winning, while the US remains opposed because it fails to address the nuclear program and asserts Iranian control over the Strait of Hormuz.

President Trump has decided to continue a long-term naval blockade on Iran instead of escalating military action or ending the conflict, according to the Wall Street Journal, solidifying a sustained maximum-pressure strategy.

The IRGC claims it recovered and neutralized multiple U.S. bombs after recent strikes, including more than 15 heavy missiles in the south, approximately 55 more plus thousands of bomblets in another region, and an intact GBU-57 bunker buster for potential reverse engineering.
The Iranian rial hits a new record low against the US dollar, further highlighting the severe economic strain on the country.

The Iranian rial drops to a new record low of 1.8 million IRR per USD, with the U.S.-led naval blockade costing Iran up to $500 million in lost revenue daily and annual inflation exceeding 40%, worsening economic hardship.
President Trump meets with oil executives, including Chevron's CEO, to discuss steps to continue the Iran blockade for months if needed, according to Reuters.
Defense Secretary Hegseth rejects suggestions that the Iran war is a quagmire, calling such claims a disgrace, and asserts that the US is winning.
President Trump rejects Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, according to Axios, and says he will maintain the naval blockade until a nuclear deal is reached.
Trump states the blockade is "more effective than the bombing" and that Iran is "choking like a stuffed pig."

CENTCOM has prepared a plan for a "short and powerful" wave of strikes targeting Iranian infrastructure, intended to break the negotiating deadlock, Axios reports, though President Trump had not ordered any strikes as of Tuesday.
Congressman Moulton reveals that the US sent its only minesweepers in the Gulf to Singapore weeks before the war started, raising questions about Strait of Hormuz mine countermeasure readiness.
Hegseth states that Iran's nuclear facilities have been completely destroyed, directly contradicting earlier assertions of an imminent nuclear threat as the war's justification.
Defense Secretary Hegseth accuses Iran of 'piracy' and 'terrorism' and says Iran is threatening international shipping.

Defense Secretary Hegseth, in testimony before the House Armed Services Committee, attacks Democratic and Republican critics as 'reckless, feckless, and defeatist' and calls the conflict an existential fight for American safety, comparing the two-month war to longer engagements in Iraq, Afghanistan, and Vietnam.
A Pentagon official states the Iran war has cost $25 billion so far.

The Wall Street Journal reports that Iran has entered an economic death spiral, with over 1 million people out of work, food prices rising rapidly, businesses reliant on online sales shutting down across the country, and inflation reaching 67% last month.

President Trump states he had a 'very good conversation' with Russian President Vladimir Putin, with Putin expressing interest in helping with Iran's highly-enriched uranium stockpile; Trump responded that he would rather Putin focus on ending the Ukraine war.
President Trump claims that Iran retains roughly 20% of its missile production facilities and warns the remainder could be destroyed quickly if no deal is reached.
The US military says the blockade has stranded 41 tankers with 69 million barrels of Iranian oil worth over $6 billion that Iran cannot sell.

Bloomberg reports that CENTCOM is looking to deploy the U.S. Army's Long-Range Hypersonic Weapon (Dark Eagle) to the Middle East in order to strike missile launchers that have been moved deep within Iran.
The Iranian regime has adopted IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi's hardline negotiating positions, indicating significant hardliner influence and making a near-term softening of Iran's stance unlikely.
The U.S. Central Command has readied a strike plan targeting Iranian infrastructure, with strikes expected as soon as tomorrow.

Iran is reportedly exploring alternative methods to circumvent the U.S. naval blockade, though these are considered suboptimal; the regime has accepted the risk of resumed war and has used the ceasefire to reorganize and regenerate its missile and drone forces.
The U.S. Treasury Secretary announces the seizure of $450 million in Iranian cryptocurrency.
US oil prices surge above $110 per barrel on reports that the U.S. is considering strikes on Iranian infrastructure targets.
The U.S. is reported to be considering the first-ever combat deployment of the 'Dark Eagle' hypersonic missile against Iran.
WTI crude futures trade at $110.47 as the U.S. moves toward potential new military action on Iran.
Crude oil prices neared $130 per barrel as inventories tightened and fears rose over possible new U.S. military action on Iran.

Axios reports that Trump is set to be briefed by CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper on new military options against Iran, including a short, intense strike campaign, possible control of the Strait of Hormuz to restore shipping, and a special forces mission targeting enriched uranium; Trump currently favors the naval blockade but is considering further military action if Iran does not make concessions.
Israeli Defense Minister says it is possible Israel will resume strikes on Iran soon.

Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf published an audio message via Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting emphasizing national unity and blaming the United States for Iran's dire economic conditions, an effort to deflect public anger and psychologically prepare the population for prolonged hardship and potential conflict resumption.
Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei vowed to sink American ships to the 'bottom of its waters.'
Defense Secretary Hegseth states that Iran is adopting a North Korea-style missile shield strategy to pursue nuclear weapons.
Oil prices spike overnight with WTI surpassing $105 per barrel as expectations grow that the U.S. naval blockade and Strait of Hormuz disruptions will persist.
Iranian President Pezeshkian publicly states that the naval blockade is a continuation of military operations against a nation paying the price for its resistance and independence.

Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf mockingly highlighted the length of Iran's borders to dismiss the U.S. naval blockade as impractical, addressing Defense Secretary Hegseth with a kilometer-to-mile conversion.
The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs bans travel to Iran, Lebanon and Iraq and urgently calls for its citizens in those countries to leave, citing regional developments.

Reporting indicates President Trump is seriously considering renewed combat operations against Iran, while Israeli media report CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper is set to brief the President on military options.

The Washington Post reports a senior Iranian official stated that Iran's security establishment rejects compromise on key matters, including uranium enrichment, consistent with IRGC commander Vahidi's unwillingness to make concessions on the Strait of Hormuz or the nuclear program.

Fox News reports that CENTCOM Admiral Brad Cooper has briefed President Trump on 'final blow' strike options against Iran, with assessed targets including remaining military equipment, regime/IRGC leadership, and infrastructure.

Reuters reports that a senior Trump administration official stated that for War Powers Resolution purposes, U.S. hostilities with Iran have terminated, citing a ceasefire that began April 7 and has been extended with no exchange of fire since then.
The number of oil tankers redirected to Iran with crude cargo continues to rise, according to TankerTrackers, indicating ongoing attempts to circumvent the naval blockade.
President Trump stated that Iran is asking for things he cannot agree to, signaling continued deadlock in negotiations.

President Trump stated that even hardliners in Iran want to make a deal because 'they have nothing,' assessing that economic devastation is producing a shift toward negotiation across the Iranian political spectrum.
President Trump revealed he was briefed by CENTCOM on options ranging from a devastating final strike to a negotiated deal, stating that on a human basis he would prefer a deal.
President Trump acknowledged high gasoline prices but promised that when the conflict is over there will be a world without an Iranian nuclear weapon.
President Trump stated that he would do it again and cannot let 'lunatics' have a nuclear weapon, adding that he thought the numbers would be worse.
President Trump said 'Their leaders are all gone - very sad, very fine people.'
President Trump asserted that Iran is not coming through with the kind of deal required and that the U.S. will not leave early until things are done properly.
President Trump accused Iran of trying to hold up the world by closing the Strait of Hormuz for years.
A Washington Post-ABC-Ipsos poll found that 61% of Americans call the war with Iran a mistake, with disapproval reaching levels comparable to the Iraq War at its peak.
President Trump stated that oil prices will drop once the war with Iran is over.
President Trump expressed dissatisfaction with Iran's latest proposal, citing continued Iranian inflexibility on nuclear and Strait of Hormuz issues.
The White House confirms that Iran has submitted a fresh proposal for another round of talks, but President Trump is not satisfied with it.
Multiple drones were reported over Iran in recent days, signaling ongoing ISR or pre-targeting activity amid tensions.
Surging jet fuel prices amid the Iran conflict have derailed Spirit Airlines' attempt to emerge from bankruptcy, costing the airline an additional $10–15 million per week in fuel expenses.

Strikes disrupted IRGC-linked cryptocurrency mining operations, which had been a major driver of Iran's power blackouts; the reduction in mining demand led to temporary stabilization of the electricity grid and surplus power.
President Trump again emphasized the lack of clarity over who is leading Iran, stating that fragmented authority complicates negotiations.

Iran's latest proposal reportedly maintains its previous stance on management of the Strait of Hormuz and its nuclear program, with some regime elements calculating that economic and political pressure could coerce U.S. concessions.
Iran has begun reducing oil production as its storage capacity reaches its limits, a step likely to prevent permanent damage to oil fields amid the blockade.
Hezbollah posted footage showing domestic drone production, amid Israeli assessments that the group is manufacturing first-person view drones, adding a regional dimension to the conflict.
President Trump stated there is a 'possibility' of resuming strikes against Iran.
Channel 12 reports that Israeli Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir is intensifying contacts with U.S. CENTCOM chief Brad Cooper on potential military action against Iran.
President Trump states he would like to eliminate the remaining 15% of Iran's missile-making capabilities, signaling continued military objectives beyond current destruction.

Iran submitted a 14-point proposal to the United States outlining a two-stage plan: first, negotiate a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end wars in Iran and Lebanon; second, begin talks on Iran's nuclear program, according to Axios.

items.title: 伊朗内部：强硬派主导谈判立场，核协议预期降温
items.description: 伊朗政权内部的强硬路线仍占上风，围绕防空能力、核谈判和外交让步的信号相互矛盾。市场此前对核协议的乐观预期正在减弱，说明外部压力并未换来清晰的妥协路径。
items.rawSummary: Iran has proposed a phased de-escalation roadmap to the U.S., while President Trump remains unsatisfied and maintains a naval blockade, as internal hardliner dominance persists and both sides brace for possible renewed military action.
items.analysis: The diplomatic standoff continues, with Iran's latest proposal, reported by Axios, outlining a phased roadmap that would first seek a 30‑day de‑escalation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, lift the naval blockade, and halt fighting across Iran and Lebanon, deferring nuclear negotiations to a second stage. This follows a 14‑point counterproposal submitted through Pakistani mediation that demanded a comprehensive settlement within 30 days, including U.S. military withdrawal, sanctions relief, compensation, and new Strait of Hormuz rules; President Trump said he cannot imagine accepting that plan and warned that combat operations remain a possibility, while describing the blockade as “very friendly” and criticizing Congress. Economic pressure is deepening, with U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent citing hard currency shortages and rationing, costs approaching $50 billion, and Iran attempting to redirect oil exports and food imports via the Caucasus while the U.S. imposes additional sanctions. Inside the regime, Foreign Minister Araghchi is reportedly acting in coordination with IRGC commander Vahidi, sidelining moderate figures, and the IRGC military wing has effectively taken over decision‑making; Tehran also announced the execution of two individuals for spying for Mossad. Israel is preparing for a potential imminent U.S. strike and a possible preemptive Iranian attack, with its Chief of Staff coordinating with CENTCOM.

keyPoints.point: The White House stated the U.S. does not consider Iran's seizure of two ships to be a violation of the ceasefire and clarified that public reports of a firm 3-5 day deadline are not true.
The White House reiterated the U.S. demand for Iran to turn over its enriched uranium.
U.S. officials identified a complete split within the Iranian leadership between moderates pushing for talks and hardliners taking a hardline approach.
Unconfirmed reports of explosions and air defense activity east of Tehran were attributed by Iranian sources to military exercises and air defense tests.

A pro-regime protest in Tehran featured the Spanish flag, signaling international solidarity with Iran's anti-U.S. stance, as Spain refused a U.S. request to use its military bases and closed its airspace to U.S. aircraft.

Reports indicate that Mojtaba Khamenei has undergone three surgeries on one leg and may require a prosthetic, and also suffered severe burns and hand surgery, permanently maiming him and raising questions about leadership succession.

The United States intercepted and boarded a sanctioned oil tanker in the Indian Ocean and redirected three Iranian-flagged tankers near India, Malaysia, and Sri Lanka, expanding the maritime blockade far beyond the Gulf of Oman.
Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf resigned from the negotiating team after reported intervention by the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, underscoring hardliner dominance.
New reports of air defense activity over Parand in Tehran province indicated heightened readiness.
Reports emerged that Iran's air defense was firing at hostile targets in Tehran, though Israeli officials denied any involvement, suggesting the activity may be performative for pro-regime marches.
An explosion was reported in the Sattarkhan district of Tehran, adding to unconfirmed incidents in the capital.
Iran announced it has decided not to enter negotiations with the US and denied making any request for direct talks, per state-aligned Tasnim news agency.
Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman stated no meeting is planned between Iran and the U.S., and any communication will be relayed through Pakistan.

The U.S. Treasury's OFAC announced new sanctions targeting Iran's oil trade and shadow fleet, including sanctions on China-based refinery Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian), 19 tankers, and crypto wallets used by the Central Bank of Iran.
Iran stated it still has significant missile capabilities that have not been used yet, signaling continued escalation capacity.

Analysis indicates that pragmatic officials may continue advocating for flexibility but are unlikely to shape regime decision-making near-term, with IRGC commander Vahidi's victory over Ghalibaf likely impacting future US-Iran negotiations.
Imam Khamenei International Airport in Tehran reopened to limited flights.
Iranian negotiators reportedly passed messages to the US asking President Trump to tone down his threats, believing that hardliners would be more open to negotiations if American pressure eased.
Iran proposed a deal to the U.S. to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, extend a ceasefire, and postpone nuclear negotiations until later, signaling a more concrete diplomatic outreach.

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that incorrect approaches and excessive demands by the U.S. caused the previous round of talks to fail despite progress, publicly acknowledging negotiations while shifting blame to Washington.

European Commission President von der Leyen said it is too early to lift sanctions on Iran, insisting that fundamental change in Iran must come first, complicating Tehran's efforts to court European allies and gain sanctions relief.

Iran's new offer to mediators reportedly outlines a 3-phase peace plan beginning with ending the war and ensuring it does not resume, and explicitly mentions Iran's intent to retain control over the Strait of Hormuz.
Smuggled footage published by the New York Post shows six protesters being executed while defiantly singing, exposing the regime's violent suppression of internal dissent.

Trump and his national security team are skeptical of Iran's latest proposal, questioning whether it is acting in good faith and willing to end uranium enrichment, but the White House will continue talks and is expected to present counterproposals, per the Wall Street Journal.

ISW analysis indicates Iran is exploiting its Strait of Hormuz leverage to secure an end to the U.S. blockade without making nuclear concessions, a push partly driven by rapidly depleting oil storage capacity forced by the blockade; IRGC commander Vahidi's support for the proposal remains unclear.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi returned to Tehran after meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg.
Trump is unhappy with Iran's latest proposal because it delays nuclear negotiations, and the U.S. insists nuclear issues must be addressed immediately, leaving both sides far apart, per Reuters.

Iran's deputy Defence Minister Brigadier General Reza Talaei-Nik stated, via state-aligned Tasnim, that the US is no longer in a position to dictate policies and that Iran is ready to share its defensive military capabilities with Shanghai Cooperation Organization members.
Several advisors privately told Trump that only resuming military action would break the deadlock with Iran.
An Israeli official stated after a high-level security briefing that the Iranian regime is about to pay a very heavy price, calling for patience and alertness.

A photo circulated showing an Iranian woman mocking the Islamic regime's 'feminist propaganda' by wearing a hijab and holding a TV frame reading IRGC TV propaganda, referencing recent women-only rallies in Tehran featuring pink military vehicles and weapons in an attempt to appeal to Western audiences.

U.S. intelligence agencies are assessing how Iran might respond if Trump declares victory and scales back the war, with early assessments suggesting Iran could see a U.S. withdrawal as a win, per Reuters.
Iran has used the ceasefire to recover and redeploy launchers, drones, and munitions previously buried by U.S. and Israeli strikes, per Reuters.

The U.S. Treasury Department announced additional sanctions targeting Iranian banking networks that fund the regime and the IRGC, including private companies known as 'Rahbars' that assist blacklisted banks in using shadow banking to support the Armed Forces General Staff, National Iranian Oil Company, and IRGC.
President Trump posted on Truth Social stating "NO MORE MR. NICE GUY!" and that Iran "better get smart soon," urging Iran to sign a non-nuclear deal.

Sources inside Iranian leadership told Reuters that the IRGC military wing has completely taken over military and political decision-making, with the newly appointed leader only able to ratify decisions rather than issue directives.
Trump's advisors told him a nuclear deal with Iran is unlikely, and Trump instructed them to prepare for an indefinite blockade until Iran capitulates, per the Wall Street Journal.

The new leadership structure is described as a collective wartime leadership centered on the IRGC and Supreme National Security Council, with Mojtaba Khamenei as nominal supreme leader endorsing decisions but not making them, and hardline military figures now driving policy, per Reuters.

Former Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, previously ousted from the negotiating team by the IRGC, stated the enemy has entered a new phase aiming to activate maritime blockade, media warfare, economic pressure, and internal division to weaken or collapse the country from within.
Senior Iranian official Mohsen Rezaee stated Iran will not tolerate the naval blockade and warned that if it continues, Iran will respond.
Iranian Navy Chief stated that a weapon they deeply fear will soon be revealed at their doorstep.
Unconfirmed reports of explosions in Iran, including Tehran, with the cause unclear at this stage.
Iran's Navy Commander warned that Iran will soon confront its enemies with a 'very dreadful weapon.'

Iran's upcoming proposal to the U.S. is expected to refuse meaningful concessions on the Strait of Hormuz and nuclear program, as the regime coalesces behind IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi's hardline approach.
Oman rejected an Iranian proposal to involve it in a toll-collection scheme aimed at legitimizing Iran's control over the Strait of Hormuz.
Significant air-defense activity and explosions were reported over Tehran; both U.S. and Israeli officials denied renewed strikes against Iran.
The U.S. Army is reportedly considering contingency plans to seize Iran's enriched uranium stockpile.
A Pentagon official said the US war against Iran has cost $25 billion so far.
Professor Robert Pape assessed that Iran is likely laying the groundwork for nuclear weapons, working with Pakistan and Russia, and positioning itself as a major center of global power.
German Chancellor Merz demanded that Iran stop playing for time, end its military nuclear program, and cease strikes against Israel and regional partners.
Reportedly, Iran's leadership seeks the removal of Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi over the handling of nuclear negotiations.
The UAE called on its citizens to immediately depart Iran, Iraq, and Lebanon.
US officials told CBS News that the true cost of the Iran war is closer to $50 billion, exceeding an earlier Pentagon estimate of $25 billion.
President Trump stated that the blockade on Iran has been '100% effective'.
Air defense activity was reported over southern Tehran.
Iranian air defense was reportedly intercepting reconnaissance drones and quadcopters in the skies over Tehran.
Polymarket estimated a 33 percent chance of a permanent US-Iran peace deal by June 30, reflecting market skepticism amid the ceasefire and blockade.
President Trump threatened to seize Iran's nuclear material by force and claimed that Iranian leaders are dead and Tehran has no functioning air defense.
Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei declared that Iran will retain control over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and maintain its nuclear and missile capabilities.

Two informed sources reported that Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has been acting in full coordination with IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi and following his instructions, while Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf and President Pezeshkian are reportedly dissatisfied with this alignment.

Polymarket odds of a nuclear deal with Iran by the end of 2026 fell sharply to 53 percent, down over 15 percentage points in a day, amid rising oil prices and growing likelihood of renewed US-Iran hostilities.
President Trump was briefed by U.S. Central Command Commander Admiral Brad Cooper on military options with Iran.
EuroPost noted that Trump's assertions about Iran's air defenses and leadership have not been independently verified.
Iran called on Gulf states to pay damages, accusing them of aiding the U.S. and Israel in the war.
The Wall Street Journal reported that Iran is attempting to redirect 40 percent of its oil exports by rail to China and import food through the Caucasus mountains to circumvent the naval blockade.

Moderate factions reportedly believe seeking a deal now with a Trump administration eager to exit the war could yield favorable terms, while hardline military factions argue for renewed hostilities to further raise oil prices and pressure Washington.
Iran sent a new peace proposal to the U.S. on Thursday, but sources said it still does not address enrichment issues or proxy support, per Reuters.
U.S. Envoy Witkoff reportedly sent amendments to restore nuclear terms, including a requirement that Iran not move enriched uranium or restart bombed sites during talks.
The U.S. Treasury issued new Iran-related sanctions.
A fire was reported in western Tehran.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent stated that the U.S. has complete control of the Strait of Hormuz, there is a hard currency shortage, food and gasoline rationing, the international community has turned against Iran, and the blockade will continue until pre-February 27 freedom of navigation is restored.
President Trump stated he is not satisfied with Iran's latest peace proposal and doubted a deal will be reached, describing Iran's leadership as very disjointed with multiple groups.
Trump claimed that even hardliners in Iran want to make a deal because they have nothing.
Trump stated that talks with Iran are being conducted by phone.
Trump expressed displeasure with Italy and Spain, claiming they feel it is acceptable for Iran to have a nuclear weapon.

The Wall Street Journal reported that Iran has eased its stance to restart peace talks, dropping its demand that the U.S. lift the blockade before negotiations and proposing simultaneous discussion of the Strait of Hormuz and sanctions relief, though the two sides remain far apart on its nuclear program.
Iran announced the execution of two people convicted of spying for Israel's Mossad.

Channel 12 reported that Israel is preparing for the possibility of an imminent U.S. strike on Iran and a potential preemptive Iranian attack, with the Israeli Chief of Staff having contacted CENTCOM Commander Cooper to coordinate.

Iran submitted a 14-point counterproposal to the U.S. through Pakistani mediation, per Tasnim, demanding a complete end to the war within 30 days, including withdrawal of U.S. forces, lifting the naval blockade, sanctions relief, compensation, and new Strait of Hormuz rules, while the U.S. had proposed a 2-month ceasefire.
President Trump stated that resuming combat operations against Iran remains a possibility.

President Trump described the naval blockade as 'very friendly' and unchallenged, and criticized Congress for actions he said hurt his negotiating ability, while responding to a reporter's question about his letter to Congress stating that hostilities with Iran have been terminated.
President Trump stated he will review Iran's plan but cannot imagine it would be acceptable.

Axios reported that Iran proposed a phased roadmap to the U.S., with an initial 30-day de-escalation phase to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, lift the naval blockade, and halt fighting, followed by a second phase of nuclear negotiations.

items.title: 美国侧面：油价与战争成本正在倒逼政策选择
items.description: 美国国内也在承受中东战事外溢压力。WIRE 信息显示，油价高位运行、战争成本估算上升，同时白宫仍在听取新的对伊朗打击和地面行动选项。对华盛顿而言，军事压力、国内成本和外交回旋空间正在同时收紧。
items.rawSummary: President Trump notified Congress that Iran hostilities have terminated, as the U.S. contends with deepening economic aftershocks — surging fuel costs, an airline bankruptcy, depleted military stockpiles, and a rising Treasury cash balance — alongside investigations into the White House Correspondents' Dinner attempted assassination and a range of other domestic and international developments.
items.analysis: President Trump notified Congress that hostilities with Iran that began on February 28 have terminated, a declaration that followed a CENTCOM briefing on new military options and occurred amid reported air defense activity over Tehran. The economic aftershocks continue to deepen: the average U.S. gasoline price surged to $4.43 per gallon — a 61% increase since December — projecting an additional $90 billion in annual consumer fuel spending, while the war's estimated cost reached $25 billion and missile stockpile depletion led Washington to warn NATO allies of delivery delays, with the Financial Times reporting that U.S. weapons shipments to the UK, Poland, Lithuania, and Estonia are now being delayed. On the fiscal front, the Treasury General Account rose to approximately $1 trillion, its highest since April 2021, driven by spring tax collections that briefly pushed total federal debt below $39 trillion, though T-bill issuance is expected to accelerate again as seasonal cash inflows slow. Domestically, Spirit Airlines filed for bankruptcy and ceased operations, prompting a federal relief plan with fare caps and preferential hiring by other carriers, while the White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting suspect faces attempted assassination charges and released videos show the gunman breaching security and shooting a Secret Service officer. Additional strains include a 25% tariff on EU auto imports, Chinese naval deployments near the Philippines, stalled Taiwan defense funding, a partial DHS funding resolution that excludes ICE and Border Patrol, Rep. Randy Fine's public declaration opposing Armenian service in Congress, and State Department approval of over $8.6 billion in military sales to Israel, Qatar, Kuwait, and the UAE.

items.title: 英国伦敦：犹太机构安全警戒升高
items.description: 伦敦犹太机构仍处于较高威胁环境中。WIRE 信息显示，此前纵火未遂和 Golders Green 袭击事件后，相关嫌疑人已被起诉，英国恐怖主义威胁级别也被上调。宗教场所安全正在成为英国国内安全议题。
items.rawSummary: An attempted arson at Kenton United Synagogue, a stabbing in Golders Green, and a thwarted embassy plot have driven the UK to raise its terror threat level to severe, with multiple arrests and a political backlash underscoring the ongoing acute risk to London's Jewish institutions.
items.analysis: The attempted arson at Kenton United Synagogue in April led to two arrests and a broader counter-terrorism sweep of eight suspects over alleged Iran-linked plots. A knife attack in Golders Green on April 29 left two Jewish men wounded, and Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamia claimed responsibility; the group has previously targeted Jewish communities across Western Europe. The attacker, Essa Suleiman, a 45-year-old British national born in Somalia, was already known to the Prevent radicalisation programme, and on May 1 he was charged with two counts of attempted murder. The UK raised its terrorism threat level to 'severe' on April 30, with officials warning further attacks are highly likely; the U.S. Embassy in London subsequently stated that the increase is driven by a rise in both Islamist and extreme right-wing terrorist threats, and on May 1 the embassy released an alert warning Americans to stay alert, reiterating the high likelihood of an attack. Separately, Abdullah Albadri, who arrived in the UK by small boat 16 days earlier, was found guilty of preparing an attack on the Israeli Embassy after being caught with two knives attempting to climb into the embassy; he had previously been deported from the UK. In the political aftermath, Sharren Haskel accused Zack Polanski of legitimizing violence after his response to the Golders Green stabbing drew criticism; Polanski later apologized, saying he had shared a post in haste. This sequence of events underscores an ongoing acute risk to Jewish institutions in London, including the previously targeted synagogue and diplomatic premises.

keyPoints.point: British police arrested a 17-year-old boy and a 19-year-old man over an attempted arson attack on the Kenton United Synagogue in northwest London.
British counter-terrorism police arrested eight individuals linked to a series of targeted attacks on Jewish sites across London, with potential links to Iran under investigation.
At least two Jewish men were stabbed in an attack in Golders Green; the suspect was arrested and one victim was left in critical condition.
Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamia claimed responsibility for the London stabbing; the group has previously targeted Jewish communities across Western Europe.
Prime Minister Keir Starmer chaired an emergency COBR meeting in response to the Golders Green stabbing attack on the Jewish community.
The Golders Green attacker was identified as a 45-year-old British national born in Somalia.
British counter-terrorism police confirmed the Golders Green attacker was already known to the government's Prevent radicalisation programme.
The UK raised its terrorism threat level to 'severe', warning that further attacks are highly likely following the London attack.
The Golders Green attacker, Essa Suleiman, a British national born in Somalia, was charged with two counts of attempted murder.

Abdullah Albadri, who arrived in the UK by small boat 16 days earlier, was found guilty of preparing an attack on the Israeli Embassy in London after being caught with two knives attempting to climb into the embassy; he had previously been deported from the UK.
The U.S. Embassy in London stated that the raised UK terrorism threat level was driven by a rise in Islamist and extreme right-wing terrorist threats.
The U.S. Embassy in London warned U.S. citizens in the UK to stay alert after Britain raised its terrorism threat level to 'severe' (second-highest).
Sharren Haskel accused Zack Polanski of legitimizing violence after his response to the Golders Green stabbing drew criticism; Polanski later apologized, saying he had shared the post in haste.

items.rawSummary: The UAE is recalibrating its foreign and security policies, marked by its withdrawal from OPEC, a travel ban on Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq, resumed air operations, and now a state security referral over an alleged arms smuggling network to Sudan.
items.analysis: The UAE is managing multiple post-conflict adjustments. Israel's military support, including Spectro and Iron Beam systems alongside Iron Dome batteries and personnel under Operation Roaring Lion, provided overt coordination during Iranian attacks, coinciding with a U.S. F/A‑18 buildup at Al Dhafra and Iranian-Omani talks on Strait of Hormuz security. The UAE Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure announced its withdrawal from OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1, citing Hormuz constraints to limit market disruption, and officials framed it as part of a broader strategic reassessment of global organisations amid tensions with Saudi Arabia. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs banned citizens from traveling to Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq, ordering immediate returns. Airports and airspace returned to normal operations. In a separate development, the UAE Attorney General referred 13 defendants and 6 companies to the State Security Court over an alleged Muslim Brotherhood-linked network that smuggled weapons and ammunition to Sudan's army, after intercepting a shipment disguised as humanitarian aid.

keyPoints.point: U.S. forces deployed 12 F/A-18s, 7 tankers, and a C-17 to Al Dhafra Air Base.
Axios reported that Israel secretly deployed its Iron Dome system and troops to the UAE during the Iran war, marking its first use abroad.
Western media reported that Netanyahu ordered the Iron Dome deployment after a call with Emirati President Mohammed bin Zayed, with several dozen IDF personnel operating the system.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi traveled to Muscat to discuss Strait of Hormuz security with Omani Sultan Haitham al Tariq.
Israel's deployment to the UAE was reportedly carried out under the name Operation Roaring Lion.
UAE announced it will leave OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1, ending its 59-year membership.
UAE Energy Minister stated the withdrawal from OPEC will not hugely impact the market because of constraints on the Strait of Hormuz.
UAE announced it will significantly increase oil production after leaving OPEC, no longer bound by production quotas.

UAE officials said the country is reviewing its role in global organisations but has no plans for further exits, describing it as a broader strategic reassessment amid tensions with Saudi Arabia and post-Iran war shifts.
US President Trump called the UAE's withdrawal from OPEC 'great' and described President Mohamed bin Zayed as 'very smart'.
UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced a travel ban on its citizens to Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq, ordering Emiratis already there to leave immediately amid current regional developments.

The Financial Times reported that Israel also supplied a Spectro drone-detection system and an Iron Beam laser air-defense system to the UAE during the Iranian attacks, alongside Iron Dome batteries and intelligence sharing.
UAE airports and airspace resumed normal operations after recent disruptions.

UAE Attorney General referred 13 defendants and 6 UAE companies to the State Security Court over an alleged Muslim Brotherhood-linked network that smuggled weapons and ammunition to Sudan's army, after intercepting a shipment disguised as humanitarian aid.

items.title: 一处海外风险点：WIRE 监测到新的重要变化
items.description: WIRE 将该事件标记为强度 4/5，累计提及 4 次。相关摘要显示局势仍在变化，建议发布前结合结构化数据再做事实核对。
items.rawSummary: Israel is expanding its air force with new F-35 squadrons and planned fighter jet purchases while receiving continued U.S. military resupply, as the country's economy outpaces G7 nations and tensions rise over a potential U.S. strike on Iran.
items.analysis: The United States conducted a large-scale resupply operation to Israel, delivering about 6,500 tons of weapons and equipment within 24 hours via ships and aircraft, including munitions, military trucks, and JLTV armored vehicles. CNBC reported that Israel is on track to outgrow every G7 economy this year, with unemployment at 3.2%, inflation below 2%, and significant gains in the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange and the shekel, driven by a dominant tech sector and surging foreign investment. In a further expansion of military capabilities, Israel has approved a fourth F-35 squadron, expanding its stealth fighter fleet to approximately 100 aircraft, while the defense ministry announced plans to purchase additional F-35 and F-15 jets from the United States. Channel 12 reported that large shipments of ammunition and military equipment have arrived recently, as Israel prepares for the possibility of a U.S. attack on Iran and the risk of an Iranian preemptive strike.

keyPoints.point: Approximately 6,500 tons of U.S. weapons and equipment, including munitions and armored vehicles, arrived in Israel within 24 hours via ships and aircraft.
CNBC reported that Israel's economy is growing faster than every G7 economy, with unemployment at 3.2%, inflation below 2%, and significant stock market and currency gains.

Channel 12 reported that large shipments of ammunition and military equipment have arrived in recent days, as Israel prepares for the possibility of a U.S. attack on Iran and the risk of an Iranian preemptive strike.
Israel approved a fourth F-35 squadron, expanding its fleet to approximately 100 aircraft.
Israel's defense ministry announced approval of a plan to purchase new F-35 and F-15 fighter jets from the United States.

items.title: 俄罗斯能源设施：炼油厂与出口终端安全压力上升
items.description: 俄罗斯能源基础设施继续处在战争外溢风险之中。WIRE 信息显示，炼油厂和出口终端相关事件受到关注，说明乌克兰远程打击与俄罗斯后方防护之间的攻防仍在持续。能源设施一旦反复受袭，可能进一步影响区域燃料供应和市场预期。
items.rawSummary: Fire at Russia's largest Baltic oil export terminal after reported drone attack
items.analysis: Multiple fires were detected at Russia's largest Baltic oil export terminal in Primorsk, with NASA's FIRMS fire monitoring system confirming the detections. The fires occurred after Ukrainian drones reportedly targeted the area, though Russian officials have not yet issued a statement. At least one loading pier was seen ablaze. The strike on a critical energy export hub marks a notable escalation in the conflict's geographic reach.

keyPoints.point: Fires break out at Port of Primorsk oil terminal following a reported Ukrainian drone attack; NASA FIRMS detects multiple fires and at least one loading pier is seen burning.

items.title: 亚丁湾：商船遭武装小艇接近
items.description: 亚丁湾方向出现航运安全信号。WIRE 信息显示，商船附近出现武装小艇接近报告。虽然事件热度不高，但该水域连接红海、印度洋和能源运输线，任何袭扰都可能影响航运风险定价。
items.rawSummary: Oil tanker hijacked off Yemen coast
items.analysis: An oil tanker was hijacked off the coast of Yemen, according to reports. The identity of the perpetrators and the condition of the crew were not immediately known. The incident is the latest in a series of maritime security threats in the Gulf of Aden region. This area is a critical chokepoint for global oil transit.
items.locationName: Off the coast of Yemen, Gulf of Aden

keyPoints.point: An oil tanker was hijacked off the coast of Yemen.

items.title: 加沙：海上拦截与陆上限制并行，人道空间继续收缩
items.description: 以色列拦截了驶向加沙的船只，同时加沙陆上限制区域继续扩大。WIRE 信息显示，军事行动、内部武装冲突传闻和对伊朗局势的讨论交织在一起，使加沙的人道和安全环境继续承压。
items.rawSummary: In the West Bank, settler violence drew a Holocaust comparison from a former Mossad director, while an Israeli unit suspended for assaulting a CNN team returned to duty, a nun was shoved at King David’s Tomb, flotilla operatives were interrogated, and Israel approved a major fighter jet purchase ahead of a security cabinet meeting.
items.analysis: Former Mossad Director Tamir Pardo compared settler violence in the West Bank to persecution of Jews in the previous century, citing his mother’s Holocaust experience. An Israeli military unit suspended for assaulting and detaining a CNN team has returned to duty, with an investigation opened but no further discipline announced, according to CNN. In Jerusalem, a Catholic nun was shoved to the ground at King David’s Tomb and a suspect was arrested for racist assault. Two flotilla operatives arrested en route to Gaza arrived in Israel, where the Foreign Ministry said they would be interrogated for suspected terrorist ties and illegal activity. The security cabinet is set to convene Sunday evening, while Israel also approved a major purchase of F-35 and F-15IA fighter jet squadrons for tens of billions of shekels.

keyPoints.point: Tamir Pardo, former Mossad director, toured settler violence sites in the West Bank and said the scenes reminded him of the events of the previous century against Jews.
An Israeli military unit that had been suspended for assaulting and detaining a CNN team returned to duty; an investigation was opened but no further discipline is known, CNN reported.
A Catholic nun was shoved to the ground at King David’s Tomb in Jerusalem; a suspect was arrested for racist assault.

Two flotilla operatives arrested en route to Gaza arrived in Israel; the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs said they will be interrogated for suspected ties to a terrorist organization and illegal activity.
Israel’s security cabinet is scheduled to convene on Sunday at 8 PM.
Israel approved buying two new fighter jet squadrons—F-35 Lightning II and F-15IA—for tens of billions of shekels.

items.title: 霍尔木兹海峡：封锁僵局继续推高能源与航运压力
items.description: 美国海上封锁仍在持续，伊朗方面拒绝把核谈判与重新开放通道直接绑定。WIRE 信息显示，英国海军确认战争爆发以来相关船舶通行量已大幅下降，布伦特原油价格仍处在高位。能源、航运和外交谈判正在相互牵动，这是今天最值得关注的全球风险点。
items.rawSummary: Kuwait recorded zero crude oil exports in April 2026 for the first time since the Gulf War, a halt linked to a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, with production continuing and oil stored or refined domestically.
items.analysis: Kuwait reported zero crude oil exports for April 2026, the first such month since the 1991 Gulf War. The export halt has been attributed by vessel tracking data to a blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, through which most regional oil shipments must transit. Production reportedly continued during the month, with crude oil either placed into storage or processed in domestic refineries instead of being shipped abroad. As a major OPEC producer, the disruption could have significant implications for global energy supply chains and regional stability.

keyPoints.point: Kuwait reports zero crude oil exports for April 2026, its first zero-export month since the end of the Gulf War in 1991.
The export halt is linked to a Strait of Hormuz blockade; production continued with oil being stored or refined domestically.

items.title: 马里首都巴马科：安全压力、物资短缺和通胀风险叠加
items.description: 马里安全形势继续恶化。WIRE 信息显示，近期袭击造成高层伤亡后，巴马科面临围困压力和国际撤离提醒；与此同时，能源和物资紧张可能进一步加剧停电、短缺与通胀问题。
items.rawSummary: A UAE-owned oil tanker, M/T Eureka, was reportedly hijacked by Somali pirates off Yemen's Shabwa coast, as stated by the Yemeni coast guard, marking the third such incident in recent times.
items.analysis: Initial reports indicated that Somali pirates hijacked a Yemeni oil tanker off the Shabwa coast, the third vessel targeted in a series of recent incidents. The Yemeni coast guard subsequently provided details identifying the seized vessel as the UAE-owned tanker M/T Eureka, which had left Fujairah eight days earlier and anchored near Al Mukallah two days before the hijacking. The claims underscore growing concerns about a possible resurgence of piracy off East Africa, though independent verification of the hijacking and the pirates' identity remains limited.

keyPoints.point: A Yemeni oil tanker was hijacked off the Shabwa coast, with Somali pirates reportedly responsible, in what is said to be the third hijacking in recent times.
The Yemeni coast guard reported that the hijacked vessel is the UAE-owned oil tanker M/T Eureka, which left Fujairah eight days earlier and anchored near Al Mukallah two days prior.

items.title: 英国伯明翰：体育馆因可疑包裹疏散
items.description: 英国伯明翰出现一起低热度但值得注意的安全事件。WIRE 信息显示，Utilita Arena Birmingham 因可疑包裹进行疏散，拆弹小组到场处置。此类事件未必会演变为重大新闻，但能反映欧洲城市公共空间的安保敏感度。
items.rawSummary: A suspicious package at the Utilita Arena in Birmingham prompted an evacuation during a Peter Kay comedy show, and a 19-year-old was subsequently arrested on suspicion of a bomb hoax.
items.analysis: The Utilita Arena in Birmingham was evacuated during a Peter Kay show after a suspicious package was discovered. A bomb squad arrived at the scene as a precaution. The day after the evacuation, a 19-year-old was arrested on suspicion of a bomb hoax offence. The incident occurred amid a heightened terrorism threat level in the UK following a recent attack in London, though the arrest was specifically for a suspected hoax.

keyPoints.point: Utilita Arena in Birmingham evacuated and bomb squad dispatched after a suspicious package was found during a comedy show.
A 19-year-old was arrested on suspicion of a bomb hoax offence following the evacuation.

items.title: 乌克兰：俄军大规模无人机袭击凸显战场消耗升级
items.description: 俄军夜间发动大规模无人机袭击，WIRE 信息显示单次出动规模达到 206 架。与此同时，地面战斗和外部军援继续推进，乌方获得包括 F-16 模拟器和资金释放在内的新支持。战场正在继续向远程打击和防空消耗倾斜。
items.rawSummary: Stalled Greece-Ukraine naval drone co-production deal
items.analysis: A 2025 agreement for Greece and Ukraine to co-produce Ukrainian naval drones in Greek shipyards has stalled. Ukrainian officials are seeking a formal say, possibly including veto power, over how Greece could deploy the drones in a conflict. Greek officials suspect Ukraine is trying to avoid antagonizing Türkiye, a key Black Sea player and mediator with Russia. The development was reported by Kathimerini.

keyPoints.point: The Greece-Ukraine shipyard co-production deal for Ukrainian naval drones is stalled over Ukraine's request for a say in Greek use of the drones, including possible veto power; according to Kathimerini, Greek officials believe Ukraine aims not to antagonize Türkiye.
